periods.label: First decade
periods.coverage_label: Volumes 1–10, through 10(2); available sample: volumes 8–9 and 10(1–2)

categories.name: Defence expenditure studies
categories.note: The editorial category includes demand, time-series properties and macroeconomic consequences of spending; the model separates a broad spending/growth topic from a narrower debt topic.
categories.definition: Demand for military expenditure, its economic consequences and the behaviour of spending over time.

categories.name: Procurement processes and policies
categories.note: Procurement is spread across the industry/industrial-base topic and the more specific equipment-cost topic. Neither topic is an exclusive procurement category.
categories.definition: How defence equipment is purchased and how procurement arrangements and incentives operate.

categories.name: Economics of alliances
categories.note: Alliance contributions, burden sharing and public goods are recognisable in the model. Similar scope does not imply identical article assignments.
categories.definition: Alliance provision and contributions, including burden sharing and public goods; later retrospectives also include common European defence cooperation.

categories.name: Conversion
categories.note: Conversion is absorbed into the broader industry topic, rather than recovered as a separate cluster.
categories.definition: The adjustment of military resources and industries towards civilian uses.

categories.name: Defence industries and industrial base
categories.note: The industry topic also captures conversion, procurement, R&D and some country surveys.
categories.definition: The structure, organisation and performance of defence producers and their industrial base.

categories.name: Military manpower
categories.note: Personnel, enlistment, labour-market and veterans research form a recognisable model topic; this topic has no assigned papers in the available first-period sample.
categories.definition: Military labour supply, recruitment, retention and the organisation of service personnel.

categories.name: Country surveys
categories.note: This is a publication format rather than a single abstract theme. Country survey IX: Spain is assigned to the industry topic; country surveys are not a distinct cluster.
categories.definition: Country-focused surveys of defence economics; a survey format rather than a single substantive topic.

categories.name: Terrorism, guerrilla warfare, and insurgencies
categories.note: The combined editorial category crosses the separate terrorism and broad conflict topics. Zero terrorism assignments in this small late-decade sample do not establish absence across the 1990s.
categories.definition: Economic analysis of terrorism and armed insurgency, combined in the original first-decade grouping.

categories.name: Defence and growth
categories.note: The broad model topic combines growth with other spending and economic-effect studies.
categories.definition: The relationship between defence expenditure and economic growth.

categories.name: Public choice and defence
categories.note: Public choice is not separately resolved by the ten-topic model; it may be present within several substantive topics.
categories.definition: Political decision making, incentives and collective choice applied to defence.

categories.name: Regional economics and defence
categories.note: Regional studies do not form a distinct model topic. This does not establish that regional research is absent.
categories.definition: Regional and local economic dimensions of defence activity and expenditure.

categories.name: Defence R&D, technological change, and weapon development
categories.note: Industrial organisation and equipment costs capture related content, but the model does not isolate R&D as an editorial category.
categories.definition: Research, technological progress and the development of military equipment.

categories.name: Military posture and strategic policy
categories.note: Strategic policy is not an independent model topic; policy content is dispersed across substantive clusters.
categories.definition: The economic dimensions of strategic choices and the configuration of military forces.

categories.name: Arms races
categories.note: The model combines arms-race, weapons-production and arms-trade content. The reviewed increasing-returns arms-race paper illustrates this overlap.
categories.definition: Strategic interaction and competitive accumulation of armaments.

categories.name: Arms trade
categories.note: The model arms topic also includes arms races and weapons production. The original first retrospective reports five trade papers; later summaries report six.
categories.definition: International transfers of weapons and the economics of arms markets.

categories.name: Disarmament and arms control
categories.note: Arms control overlaps the mixed arms topic, without being independently resolved.
categories.definition: The economics of reducing and limiting armaments.

categories.name: Others
categories.note: A residual editorial category has no one-to-one thematic model equivalent.
categories.definition: Residual papers outside the named categories; not a single research theme.

categories.name: Military production function
categories.note: Production and efficiency content overlaps industry and equipment costs, rather than forming a standalone model category.
categories.definition: The relationship between military inputs, outputs and productive efficiency.

categories.name: Nature of defence economics
categories.note: History and scope of the field are not independently resolved. The reviewed Adam Smith article illustrates content outside the dominant interpretation of the broad conflict cluster.
categories.definition: The scope and conceptual foundations of defence economics as a field.

categories.name: Defence budgets
categories.note: Budget-related content can fall within spending or debt; the model does not isolate budgeting as a category.
categories.definition: The formulation and allocation of defence budgets.

categories.name: Developing countries and defence
categories.note: The reviewed Turkey growth study illustrates a country-specific application inside the broad spending/growth topic.
categories.definition: Defence economics questions focused on developing economies.

periods.label: Second decade

categories.name: Defence and the economy
categories.note: The model spending/growth cluster also contains expenditure-demand and other macroeconomic studies that the editors separate into additional categories.
categories.definition: The broad economic impact and effects of defence expenditure, including growth and other macroeconomic outcomes.

categories.name: Terrorism
categories.note: Both groupings identify a terrorism theme. Similar counts or shares are thematic correspondence, not verified article-level agreement.
categories.definition: Economic analysis of terrorist behaviour, its consequences and counterterrorism.

categories.name: Defence policies, planning and management
categories.note: Procurement and management content is distributed across industry and equipment-cost topics; neither has the same editorial scope.
categories.definition: A broad policy grouping including procurement, budgeting and allocation, military policy and posture.

categories.name: Conflict and civil wars
categories.note: The model conflict/war/peace topic extends beyond civil wars to other conflict and peace-related work.
categories.definition: The economics of conflict and civil war, including their causes and consequences.

categories.name: Defence industries and industrial base
categories.note: The model industry topic also contains conversion, R&D, procurement and country or company surveys.
categories.definition: The structure, organisation and performance of defence producers and their industrial base.

categories.name: Peace and peacekeeping
categories.note: Peace-related work can fall within conflict or alliance topics. The model has no standalone peacekeeping cluster, so the editorial decline cannot be verified from a dedicated model series.
categories.definition: Economic analysis of peace and activities that maintain peace.

categories.name: Arms races, arms control and disarmament
categories.note: The mixed arms topic includes arms trade and production as well as arms races and control; its count is not a count of this editorial category.
categories.definition: Arms competition together with policies and agreements to constrain or reduce armaments.

categories.name: Economics of alliances
categories.note: Alliance public goods, burden sharing and contributions are recognisable; the model includes both NATO and other alliances.
categories.definition: Alliance provision and contributions, including burden sharing and public goods; later retrospectives also include common European defence cooperation.

categories.name: Defence R&D and technology
categories.note: R&D overlaps industry and equipment-cost research but does not form a separate model cluster.
categories.definition: Research and development and technological change in the defence sector.

categories.name: Fiscal effects of defence spending
categories.note: The model debt topic is a narrower fiscal theme; the editorial category also includes other budgetary and fiscal effects.
categories.definition: Public-finance consequences of military spending, rather than all macroeconomic effects.

categories.name: Military personnel and recruitment
categories.note: Recruiting, attrition, labour-market outcomes, military service and veterans research form a recognisable topic.
categories.definition: Military labour, recruitment, retention and personnel issues.

categories.name: Models of defence expenditures
categories.note: Demand and expenditure models are absorbed into the broad model spending/growth topic.
categories.definition: Modelling and explaining the determination and patterns of defence expenditure.

categories.name: Arms trade
categories.note: The model arms topic also covers arms races and control; it is not an exclusive trade category.
categories.definition: International transfers of weapons and the economics of arms markets.

categories.name: Country surveys
categories.note: Country surveys are organised by substantive abstract content. The reviewed Spain and UK surveys appear within industry, not in a distinct survey cluster.
categories.definition: Country-focused surveys of defence economics; a survey format rather than a single substantive topic.

categories.name: Others
categories.note: A residual editorial category has no one-to-one thematic model equivalent.
categories.definition: Residual papers outside the named categories; not a single research theme.

categories.name: Regional economics and defence
categories.note: The model has no distinct regional-economics topic; papers may be dispersed across broader clusters.
categories.definition: Regional and local economic dimensions of defence activity and expenditure.

method.basis: Fixed topics from the published all-period model, split by publication volume and issue; no per-decade refits.
method.model_denominator: All abstract-bearing records in the matching period, including unassigned abstracts.
method.editorial_denominator: The classified-paper total in each original retrospective, excluding separately listed book reviews.
method.crosswalk: Curated after reading period-specific representative abstracts. Mappings describe scope overlap; topic counts repeat across rows and must not be added.
method.limits: Editorial categories, ten model clusters and available abstract-bearing records are not identical classifications or populations. Similar counts are not accuracy estimates. A missing standalone cluster does not mean a research theme was absent.
